She smartly commands a garrison of more than two hundred active duty soldiers; however, due to her chaotic nature, some members of the Assembly, as well as their imperial patrons, don't fully trust the dragon, and question her true intentions. Nevertheless, Satyana is well respected by the people of New Haxon. She is also known as one of Wynandir’s foremost curators and collectors of arcane relics.

A gas grenade is a handheld weapon that delivers a cloud of noxious gas. Depending on the chemical used, the fumes may irritate mucus membranes (e.g. eyes and nose) or skin, or may have more serious effects such as rendering victims unconscious or dead. Grenades that use toxic chemicals are banned by international law, but may still see illegitimate use. Modern police and military forces may use non-lethal tear gas to disperse crowds or incapacitate combatants.

A runechild is a sorcerer whose body collects and stores arcane energy in the form of natural runes, called essence runes, which are invisible beneath the skin when not in use. As runechildren grow more powerful, more runes manifest on their body, and the first is usually on the forehead. When a runechild charges or uses the power of these runes, they shed a bright light. This power can be passed down through a bloodline. The Runechild sorcerous origin was created by Matthew Mercer and was released as part of the Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting sourcebook.

The H.C.A.R. (Heavy Counter Assault Rifle) is a modernized semi-automatic version of the World War II BAR 1918 developed by Ohio Ordnance Works, Inc. The weapon is lightweight, with a reduction almost 8 pounds compared to the BAR, and is completely customizable, but still fires the BAR's .30-06 Springfield round (7.62x63mm) and uses the same Browning 3-position gas system. The H.C.A.R. uses a pistol grip, adjustable stock, multiple Picatinny-type accessory rails and can feed from a 30-round detachable magazine, compared to the BAR's 20 round magazine.

The Gun Bench is a feature introduced in the Battlefield Hardline: Betrayal. It is available for owners of the expansion and Battlefield Premium members, accessible from the main menu on consoles and the loadout menu on Battlelog for PC. It allows players to customize up to five primary weapons with custom reticles, colors, custom camouflages, visual wear and tear, as well as a stat tracker to show how much damage has been done to the enemy. It also features a shooting range, dubbed the Gun Range, that allow players to test their newly customized weapons. All customization options are merely cosmetic and technically do not provide any gameplay advantages. Players may turn off customization from the Gun Bench in the options menu to make themselves and other players appear to them as if they are wearing normal camouflage.

The 10 kg bomb is typical of the small bombs used during the First World War. Bombs dropped from aircraft were first employed in the Italo-Turkish War of 1911 and the First Balkan War of 1912, but aerial bombardment did not become commonplace until World War I. Initially bombs were improvised from hand grenades or converted artillery shells and dropped out of an aircraft by hand onto enemy positions. By the end of the war, bomb racks under the wings and fuselage, and even early bomb sights were developed. Bombs of 10 kilograms (about 22 pounds) or less were often used for tactical bombing against targets such as enemy trench lines, supply depots, artillery batteries, and other non-fortified targets.

Gas Bombs refer to the delivery of toxic chemical agents via aircraft, usually bombers. Soon after the widespread deployment of poison gas artillery shells during World War I, chemical munitions intended to be dropped from the air were developed, however their practical use was limited due to the capacity of aircraft of the time, as the majority of gas attacks were delivered in saturation bombardments. Gas bombs saw additional use in conflicts during the interwar years, the Second Sino-Japanese War and in World War II.

A Garotte is a type of handheld assassination weapon that, when placed around a victim's neck and pulled taut, can be used to strangle a person. It is comprised of a flexible, high-tensile material such metal wire or nylon, with purpose-built garottes having handles at each end. Garottes can also be improvised from other materials such as rope, chain and telephone cables. Since World War II, the garotte has been regularly employed as weapon by soldiers as a means of silently killing sentries and other enemy personnel. Instruction in the use of both types of garrottes is included in the training of many elite military units and special forces.

Infantry refers to the branch of an army that engages in combat on foot, rather than on horseback, in vehicles, or operating a crew-served weapon. They are often the most numerous type of unit fielded, and necessary for most every conflict. By sheer numbers they effect control over territory, assets, and civilians. Infantry units can be quickly raised, trained, deployed, and maintained, but are also most susceptible to casualties, deprivation, strain, and stress. As the oldest military discipline, their tactics are the most widely recorded and studied throughout history. Though modern armies increasingly rely on motorized or mechanized forces, wherever there is a battlefield, there will always be 'boots on the ground'. Though the Battlefield series has featured infantry in every installment, only one class is specifically called "Infantry".

It was also license-manufactured by Fábrica de Braço de Prata in Portugal as the m/968 and in Mexico by SEDENA as the MG21. Praetorians are located in the first part of the raid when opening the Vault and when fighting the Gatekeepers. They are the only Vex unit that can capture Vex plates.

Reksis Vahn, the Hangman was a Scorn Baron that appears in Forsaken. He was a depraved executioner who had a strong hatred for Servitors and their place in Eliksni culture. He utilized a Flame Cauldron in combat similar to other Ravagers of the Scorn. He was imprisoned in the Prison of Elders alongside the other Scorn Barons before being set free by Uldren Sov.

The Herzog AR-Shotgun is an Assault gadget, used as an underbarrel attachment for the SCAR 11, Bofors Defense Rifle, Krylov FA-37, Voss L-AR and Baur H-AR assault rifles. It appears in Battlefield 2142. Each rifle has their own visual characteristics when using this attachment: *In the SCAR 11, the rounds in the form of a small rack are loaded into an open slot in the top of the stock. *In the Bofors, the rounds in a rectangular magazine are loaded into an opening slot located on the left side, close to the weapon's handguard. *In the Krylov, the rounds are used in a small cylinder magazine loaded directly into the underbarrel attachment featured on the weapon. *In the Voss, the rounds in a small box are mounted on the top of the stock of the weapon. *In the Bauer, the rounds in a rectangular magazine are loaded into another tilting slot like the main magazine under the weapon near the trigger.

Sylok is a Ultra Taken Knight that can be found in Level 41 Prison of Elders and Challenge of the Elders. Sylok uses a Void Boomer as his main weapon, and can also send out flaming projectiles on the floor. In Challenge of the Elders, the projectiles become even more dangerous. The projectiles are even bigger and last longer.

TR3-VR (Tame Relaxed Triple Vac Roommate), or Trevor, was a robot encountered in the Zero Hour mission in Destiny 2. TR3-VR possessed a large squarish body and a multitude of scissor-like legs. TR3-VR was capable of killing the Guardian in one hit and could easily run them down. A sinister red glow and ominous clicking sound would alert players to its presence.

Taken Goblins are Goblins have been corrupted by the Darkness and became a Taken, introduced in The Taken King. They behave identically to Goblins, but they use a tether to make a nearby ally invulnerable to damage.
In Battlefield Play4Free, the improved APC armour plating is an equipment expertise training option available for every kit. It reduces damage done to an APC from any source.
The Infantine is a Hive Ogre ultra in the Destiny: The Taken King story mission Summoner's Circle. He periodically pounds the ground, causing tremors and slowing the Guardian's movement.
Tyra Karn is a Cryptarch and a Warlock who can be found in the Iron Temple.
An Hamaat, the Warp is a Taken Wizard found in an Ascendant Challenge with An Salaak, the Weft, and has the capability to control the movement or placement of Blights.
In Battlefield Play4Free, Improved Tank Armour is a tier 2 equipment expertise training option available for every kit. When taken, it reduces damage done to the player's tank from any source.
Acasia is a Psion who was conscripted into the Acolytes of Nezarec.

Ainigmatos, Indecipherable Proto-Mind is a powerful Vex Minotaur which serves as the final boss of the Vex variant of Enigma Protocol. While possessing no unique mechanics, Ainigmatos will teleport to a different section of the stage at every seventh quarter of its health pool to evade enemy fire.

Atraks-1, Fallen Exo (formerly known as Atraks, the Wildcard) is a Fallen Baroness of the House of Salvation. She served under Eramis, Kell of Darkness as a member of her inner council, alongside Kridis, Phylaks and Praksis. After Phylaks and Praksis were defeated by the Young Wolf, Atraks was ordered by Eramis to secure the Deep Stone Crypt, where she uploaded her consciousness into an Eliksni-based Exomind. This gave Atraks the ability to duplicate herself into multiple copies, which she used to her advantage while fighting the Guardians aboard the Morning Star space station.

The Il-2 Sturmovik (Russian: Ил-2) was a Soviet ground-attack aircraft designed in the late 1930s by Ilyushin. It was produced in very large numbers during World War II: combined with its successor, the Il-10, there were over 42,000 planes built, making it the most produced aircraft ever. It was a two-man aircraft and was known to have an exceptional performance against tanks with accurate dive bombing and powerful 20, 23 or even 37 mm guns that could penetrate the tank's rear armor.
Baiish, Taken Sibling-Errant is a Taken Phalanx striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.

Baurisk, Envoy of Savathûn is the first Taken Incendior encountered by Guardians and is the head of Savathûn's incursion on a Vex supercomputer located within The Endless Gate. It is the final boss of the The Festering Core Strike, where it attempted to halt the guardians from clearing out the Blight infestation but failed and was destroyed.

Besurith, Daughter of Crota is a child of the Hive prince Crota seen in the In the Deep Mission, where she and some Scholars attempted to protect the Cryptoglyph from The Guardian. She would protect the key Hive artifact by preserving it within the Catacombs in order to help to perpetuate her sister's plan. However once the interloper reached the deepest recesses where where her and her Scholars resided, she personally attacked the Guardian to keep the Cryptoglyph from falling into their hands, resulting in her inevitable demise.

A is a non-magnifying gun sight that allows the user to look through a glass optical window and see a cross hair reticle image superimposed at a distance on the field of view. The hologram of the reticle is built into the window and is illuminated by a laser diode. The EOtech 552 and 553 models appear predominantly throughout the Battlefield series.
Barrier Servitors are powerful Fallen Champions equipped with barrier shield abilities.
Bluejay, also known by his real name, Conrad Jain, was a Cloud Strider of Neomuna.

Brood Hosts are specialized Hive Knights seen in the Broodhold Strike, where the Knights can be seen protecting their nest in the Hellrise Canyon and the Broodhold itself. Given a Worm corrupted by Ether, the Knights are both empowered and poisoned by the adverse effects of the alien substance, granted increased resilience and strength while responsible for feeding the volatile Worm inside them.

The Harrier (also known as the Jump Jet) is a family of fighter aircraft that were developed in the United Kingdom and exported to a number of nations, including the United States of America, where the USMC still use them. They are capable of Vertical/Short Takeoff and Landing (V/STOL) just like the F-35. __TOC__
The Bulwark of Xivu Arath is a Major Hive Wizard encountered on Seraph Station.
Brom, Bound is a Taken Centurion striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.
Cyrell, the Ghost Hunter was a former Guardian of The Last City turned rogue Lightbearer who murdered Ghosts that had yet to find their Guardians.

The IPS (Infantry Protection Shield) is a gadget featured in Battlefield 2142 that is available to the Support kit as an initial unlock. When deployed, the IPS erects a glowing red force shield (similar to those used inside a Titan's corridors) that resists all small arms and machine gun fire, as well as blasts from explosives. The IPS can also resist a certain number of anti-vehicle weapon rounds or large-caliber vehicle weapons before failing. The shield is sufficient to cover most of a crouch soldier from a roughly 60° arc in front. The shield cannot be passed through, moved or disturbed by other players. As such, a carefully placed IPS can prevent players from ascending a ladder or passing through small openings. It is possible to destroy an IPS with small arms and machine gun fire, but it must be very precise. Targeting the control box on the IPS will destroy it, although no damage is done visually. IPSBF2142.png|The IPS while held. IPSBF2142Deployed.png|The IPS deployed.

The Combustor Valus is a Cabal Blood Guard Incendior encountered on Mercury where they lurk in the Pariah's Refuge. Their Bounty can be picked up from the Spider as part of a weekly interval. Unlike many of his Red Legion brethren, the Combustor Valus would successfully secure a Lost Sector for himself and his forces, yet they would still fall to the Guardian regardless.

Dark Council Guards are Captains from the House of Salvation seen in the Deep Stone Crypt Raid. They are unique for their Void Absorption Shields and act as personal Guards for Dark Council members. These units are seen protecting the House of Salvation's operations within the Crypt itself and operate as a powerful reinforcements that appear in almost all encounters.

A Deathsinger is a special kind of Hive Wizard which possesses the ability to sing the Deathsong, a powerful song which kills anyone listening when it is complete. Two of them sing Crota's dirge with his sisters in Last Rites.

A hit marker or hitmarker is a visual cue that tells the player that they scored a hit and damaged an enemy with a projectile or explosion from their weapon, a vehicle's weapon or an explosive device. Hit markers have appeared in all Battlefield games.

Drake, Stasis Sniper is a Stasis-wielding Captain from the House of Salvation. Drake can be found in Kell's Rising and plays a important role in completing a Penguin Triumph and must be defeated to collect the Penguin Souvenir toy.

Descendant Axis Hobgoblins are an Elite variant of the Vex Descendant Hobgoblin. They can be distinguished from their Minor counterparts by the dark grey parts of their frame, and possess increased strength and health.

The Digital Variant Tracker is an Ultra Vex Wyvern of the Sol Collective encountered in the Variant Security Protocol node of the Vex Network. It was summoned by the system to deal with The Guardian, who was following a mysterious signal that led them deeper in the network. It confronted the Lightbearer with large amounts of reinforcements, but was slain nonetheless.

The ASRAD-R (Advanced Short Range Air Defense) is a vehicle-mounted short-range air defense system, designed by Rheinmetall Defence of Germany and Swedish Saab Bofors Dynamics. The system is modular and can be mounted on almost any wheeled or tracked vehicle. Although the system can be mounted on a single vehicle, it can also be split, with one vehicle carrying the sensor package, and other vehicles carrying missiles. The ASRAD-R is currently used by Germany, Greece, and Finland.
The Dire Minotaur is a type of Taken Minotaur which has been granted new defensive capabilities.

Eramis, Kell of Darkness (formerly known as Eramis, the Shipstealer) is the Fallen Kell of the House of Salvation and the first Eliksni to wield the power of Stasis from the Witness and the Black Fleet. Prior to that, she was a former Baroness from the House of Devils having led the united front of Fallen Houses in the Battle of the Twilight Gap. Captured and imprisoned in the Prison of Elders sometime during the Wolf Rebellion, she would escape during the mass breakout initiated by Variks and united Fallen traditionalists to create the House of Salvation and become a new "Kell of Kells". However, after her initial attempt to rally the Houses failed and her House increasingly became in the thrall of the Witness over the years, Eramis would eventually leave Sol altogether, planning on using an Echo released from the Traveler after the Witness's death to rebuild Riis. She is the main antagonist of the Beyond Light expansion and later Season of Plunder, as well as a secondary antagonist in Season of the Seraph and Season of Defiance, and an ally in Episode: Revenant.

Drekthas, Metal Captain is a Fallen Captain of the House of Dusk that serves as the main boss of the Lost Sector, The Drain. He is regarded by Taniks, the Scarred as being one of the finest Eliksni Warriors and someone more capable than Aksor, Archon Priest. As with most of their counterparts they wield a shrapnel launcher in battle and pursue Guardians in a swift and aggressive manner. This can prove deadly for unaware Guardians due to the tight, enclosed spaces of The Drain.

Special purpose SUVs in use with some SWAT forces and law enforcement agencies are outfitted with a machine gun turret for situations when greater firepower is required. Due to police rules of engagement, they are rarely used, though they are well-maintained. The Intervention SUV in Battlefield Hardline is based on the Chevrolet Tahoe.

Erruk, the Taken is a Taken Wizard encountered in the Story mission Sacrilege. They are one of the three Wizards, the others being Norr, the Taken and Wyr, the Taken, along with Irausk, Herald of Savathûn whom of which tried to take the Traveler's energy on Io. However they and their coven would be discovered and wiped out by The Guardian.
Ereshkel, Insight of Savathûn was a powerful Taken Wizard encountered in the Taken Blight Public Event during the Io Flashpoint.

The Energized Brute is a Hive Ogre seen in the Tidal Anchor, where it is being used to divert power to itself. After it's discovery, the Vanguard issued an Assassination order through Patrol and the brute was killed.

The "HK51" is blanket term for a compact variant of the Heckler & Koch G3 rifle. They are not officially made by Heckler & Koch, and are generally G3 rifles converted with short barrels and collapsible stocks, making them more maneuverable in close quarters. It fires the powerful 7.62x51mm NATO round, giving it high firepower, but the rifle's short length gives it high recoil and limited range. An HK51 appears in Battlefield Hardline, categorized as a Battle Rifle.
Enitan was a Lightbearer who operated in the Saharan Contested Zone during the Dark Age, protecting civilians from Fallen raiders under the guise of the Red Moon Phantom.
Enforcer Rao is a Psion enforcer and leader of the Totality Division crime syndicate.

Firethorn was a Ghost partnered with Briar. Briar gouged out his own eyes as an effect of Nezarec's psychic effects, leading Firethorn to restore his vision. Angered, Briar turned his knife to Firethorn and shattered him.

Improvised Firearms are firearms that are not made by weapon manufacturers or gunsmiths, and are constructed out of existing materials available to regular civilians. These weapons can range from being very crudely made weapons which are dangerous to operate to high-quality reproductions of existing firearms made from re-purposed materials. Popular in areas with strict gun-control laws, Improvised guns are generally illegal to own or create, and are commonly used by Criminals for violent crime or insurgent forces unable to acquire actual firearms. An improvised firearm based off the PA Luty design appears in Battlefield Hardline as the Improvised Gun.
Grayliks, Winter Baron is a Fallen Baron encountered in The Archive Story Mission.

Golmuut was a Hive Ogre encountered in the Cargo Bay 3 Lost Sector on Titan. Golmut was destroyed and its lost sector looted by Glimmer hungry Guardians at the request of The Spider who put a bounty on its head.

The Forgebound Cantors are special Hive Wizards seen in the Oblation Exotic Mission, they have been blessed with Soulfire abilities which make them far more dangerous than their regular counterparts. They are visually distinguishable by their central green eye on their head and the Hive symbols on their chest.

The Nissan Skyline R34 GT-R is a Japanese sports car produced between 1999 and 2002. The GT-R served as Nissan's flagship performance vehicle, and became an iconic sportscar of the 1990s despite only officially being exported to a few territories outside of Japan. The R34 was the fifth generation of the Skyline model, and introduced an 5.8" LCD display on the dash which displayed live readings of vehicle statistics, a unique feature at the time of its production. A customized racing Skyline R34 appears in Battlefield Hardline as the Import Tuner.

Hashladûn, Daughter of Crota (also known as the Inundated) is an Ascendant Hive Wizard and the eldest of the Daughters (herself, Besurith, Voshyr, and Kinox) of the Hive god Crota, Son of Oryx and Omnigul, Will of Crota, as well as granddaughter of Oryx, the Taken King. She is the leader of the Hidden Swarm and architect of the Scarlet Keep, harnessing the Nightmares of the Lunar Pyramid that lies beneath for her schemes in vengeance against the Guardians. Hashladûn would meet her end by the Guardian at the top of the Tower of Woe as part of her revenge against them, only to be killed by their fireteam.

Hadragal, Keeper of Memory is a powerful Hive Wizard of the Lucent Brood who was charged with keeping watch over the Altar of Reflection. They can be found in the Altar of Reflection: Insight Mission, where they are encountered as the final boss.

Grutuk is a Ghost of the Lucent Brood. She was employed as part of the operations outside the Court of Savathûn, where she stalked and ambushed Guardians alongside her Lightbearer Xavol. She would use her processing power to calculate the best places from which to ambush their foes.

A Hearse is a funeral vehicle used to transport a coffin from a church or funeral home to a cemetery. The base of most Hearses is generally that of more luxurious car brands, with Cadillacs and Lincolns being the most popular in the United States, with the rear of vehicle given custom bodywork to hold the coffin.

The House of Rain Servitor was a powerful Fallen Servitor encountered in the Corridors of Time Part 1 Mission. It was deployed alongside the House of Rain Walker at the Zephyr Station Perimeter to help finish off the surviving Saint-14. However, it would be destroyed by Guardian after they use Sundial to save the legendary Titan.

The House of Rain Walker is a specialized Fallen Walker seen in the Corridors of Time Part 1, where it shows up with the House of Rain Servitor at the Zephyr Station Perimeter to finish of the last survivor, the legendary Titan Saint-14. However, using the power of The Sundial to go back in time to meet with the Titan, the Walker and it's Servitor back-up would be destroyed, despite the Walker's ties to the nearby Ketch's weaponry.

Irausk, Herald of Savathûn was a Taken Centurion that appeared in the mission Sacrilege in Destiny 2. It was summoned to Io by three Taken Wizards, Norr, the Taken, Wyr, the Taken, and Erruk, the Taken, as part of an effort by the Taken to siphon the Traveler's remnant energy from the Jovian moon. Despite its best efforts, Irausk and the wizards that summoned it would be destroyed by The Guardian.
Holes Through Steel is a Codex Entry featured in Battlefield 1. It is unlocked upon obtaining 10 kills with the Tank Hunter Elite Class.
Jawar, Proxy was a Cabal Psion simulation seen in the Infinite Forest, paired with Kulam, Proxy and Moc, Proxy, they act as a Daemon firewall to inhibit any intruder's progress through the forest.

Jorin Nal is a Warlock. They kept a journal in which they wrote about their thoughts on being reborn by the Traveler, noting that while they had not asked to be resurrected or the power of the Light, they had embraced it. However, Jorin also feared they were unworthy of the power the Traveler gifted them, and felt a longing within themselves to return to a home that they no longer recalled.

Kovik's Monster was a Hive Ogre infused with SIVA by Kovik, Splicer Priest. As part of the High Priest's twisted experiments, it had its eye torn out of its socket and attached to his weapon. From then on, it would serve Kovik's bodyguard and pet project, as shown in the Wretched Eye Strike.
The Infantry Support Weapons is a Codex Entry featured in Battlefield 1. It is unlocked upon obtaining ten kills with the AT Rocket Gun.
Louis is a Peregrine Falcon, and is the animal companion of Guardian associate Suraya Hawthorne.

Kit Ali Ameir is a Hunter who had visions of the future. More than a century before the Guardians encountered the Cabal on Mars, Kit drew images of the Cabal. This mystified other Guardians who pondered how she was able to do so.
Kulam, Proxy was a Cabal Psion simulation seen in the Infinite Forest, paired with Jawar, Proxy and Moc, Proxy, they act as a Daemon firewall to inhibit any intruder's progress through the forest.
Huot Automatic Rifle is a Codex Entry featured in Battlefield 1. It is unlocked upon obtaining 10 kills with the Huot Automatic Rifle.
Lakpha was a member of the Future War Cult during the Golden Age who participated in experiments with a device based on Vex technology that allowed its user to send their mind across space and time.

Kit was a human who volunteered to be tested with a SIVA prototype, Splendor 2.6, in an effort to find an advantage in life. She began to feel exhilarated, and broke several pieces of equipment in the process. After six hours, she began reporting yellow artifacts floating at the edge of her vision. However, she remained excited about the project, and asked to perform strength and intelligence tests three times a day rather than daily. After Patient B reached a clinical state, Doctor Zarin Shirazi informed her as per policy. Kit was shocked, and questioned how she could have injected them without informing them there was a 20% mortality rate. Eventually she entered a coma, along with the other patients. Shirazi and her team worked tirelessly and developed a cure, saving Kit and the other patients. Jun, another patient enlisted Kit to help him expose Clovis Bray's unethical research.
Krissik, Bound is a Hive Wizard of Xivu Arath's Horde striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.

The Mle 1914 Hotchkiss machine gun chambered for the 8mm Lebel cartridge became the standard machine gun of the French Army during World War I. It was manufactured by the French arms company Hotchkiss et Cie, which had been established in the 1860s by American industrialist Benjamin B. Hotchkiss. The gas-actuated Hotchkiss system was first formulated in 1895 by Odkolek von Ujezda and improved into its final form by Hotchkiss armament engineers Laurence Benét and Henri Mercié. The Mle 1914 followed the Mle 1909—which saw service with British and American forces—and was the last of version of the original Mle 1897. It replaced the St. Étienne Mle 1907 as France's standard machine gun.

Malevolent Blades are rampant Hive Darkblades seen in the final encounter of the In the Deep Story Mission. They spawn once The Guardian steals the Cryptoglyph and are forced to run, when these Knights are called upon to chase after them and re-secure the Cryptoglyph back into Hive hands.

Manse-5 is a Guardian in service of the Vanguard. He received a new Sparrow from Amanda Holliday, the SV-112 Predator, and took it for a test run while patrolling the European Dead Zone. While being pursued by three Fallen Pikes he conversed with another Guardian over the radio, updating them as he used the new Sparrow's speed to cause two pikes to crash as they attempted to keep up with him and the third to crash into a Cabal ship. Excited about the capabilities of the SV-112 Predator, Manse declared that he would buy Amanda a drink when he returned to the Tower that night.

Madhir was an Ahamkara fought by Ikora Rey, presumably during the Great Ahamkara Hunt. According to Ikora, she was able to defeat Madhir by allowing him to change her into "someone [he] could not tempt," forever altering her personality as a result.

The was an automatic conversion for the Lee-Enfield rifle. It consisted of a Lee-Enfield rifle fitted with an external gas tube that operated the original Lee-Enfield bolt with a curved cam. The weapon used 20-round trench magazines. The weapon was reliable but unergonomic for the user as the force of the recoiling bolt interfered with handling.
Mihaylova is the Ghost of Micah-10. At some point, Mihaylova would assist Micah in finding a backup of her memories in a Clovis Bray facility.
Lyrix, Sacrificed by Otzot is a powerful Taken Psion encountered in the Blooming in the Pale Heart during an Overthrow event.

Mormu, Xol Spawn is a Major Hive Wizard, who appears as a mini boss in The Summoning Pits Strike. She and her coven are responsible for conducting rituals upon the Hive's Ogres including the creation of Phogoth, the Untamed.

The Hyper Drive Rifle is a weapon featured in Battlefield Heroes for the Royal Army and was introduced with the second Robots bundle on January 16, 2013. Available for the Commando kit, it is statistically identical to the National Army Elektro Slinger.

Mithrax, Kell of Light or Misraaks is an Eliksni Kell who founded the House of Light. After being spared by The Guardian on Titan when attempting to gain control of a methane reactor to boost his crew's Ether supply, Mithrax would abandon his old House and begin working with Guardians, including stopping a Devil heist to steal SIVA. Later, Mithrax helped the Guardians to end the Endless Night created by the Vex, using his abilities as a Sacred Splicer to breach the Vex network by refocusing Light. After which, he became a staunch ally of the Vanguard with his House taking up permanent residence in the Last City's Botza District. Since these events, he has become a frequent ally to both the Vanguard and one of the co-leaders of the Coalition as the Witness began to make its way to the Sol System.
Moc, Proxy was a Cabal Psion simulation seen in the Infinite Forest, paired with Kulam, Proxy and Jawar, Proxy, they act as a Daemon firewall to inhibit any intruder's progress through the forest.

The Nightmare of Jaxx, Claw of Xivu Arath is a Nightmare of a Hive Ogre that appears every four weeks at the Hellmouth as part of a weekly rotating powerful Nightmare encounter. Once an Ogre serving Xivu Arath, God of War, the Ogre was a powerful war machine widely feared before its demise. A deadly projection of Jaxx was created by the forces of the Lunar Pyramid as a deadly, yet rarely appearing foe.

Homer's Homing Gun is a light machine gun featured in Battlefield Heroes for the Royal Army. Available for the Gunner kit, it was introduced in the Battlefield Heroes: Aliens bundle on February 28, 2013. Its counterpart is Beck's Bloodhound Gun for the National Army.

The Nightmare of Xortal, Sworn of Crota is a Nightmare of a Hive Knight that appears every four weeks in Sorrow's Harbor as part of a weekly rotating powerful Nightmare encounter. Once a subordinate commander of Crota, Xortal was a mighty and widely feared warrior before his demise (presumably during The Great Disaster). During the Haunting of the Moon, the Knight would be recreated by the powers of the The Lunar Pyramid as a deadly, yet rarely appearing foe.
Nadya was a Awoken Warlock who served as a Guardian of The Last City. She was among the many Guardians who fought to free the Dreaming City of a Taken curse.

Mor'ak, Lightstealer is a Hive Lightbearer Acolyte Lieutenant who led hunting parties in the European Dead Zone to kill Guardians in order to steal their light. They are encountered as the final boss of the PsiOps Battleground: EDZ activity.

The HaChi (alternatively the Rocket Barrage Tank) is a Squad Reinforcement featured in Battlefield V, introduced in Tides of War chapter 5, War In The Pacific. A variant of the Type 97 medium tank, it is the Japanese counterpart to the US T34 Calliope. It can be called in for 20,750 requisition points. Despite its similar appearance, the HaChi can be distinguished from the regular Type 97 due to a camouflage covering of palm fronds, and is outfitted with increased firepower in the form of dumbfire rockets launched from the sides of a larger, squarer-looking turret. As the driver, HaChi operators have access to a burst-fire rocket launcher system which fires six rockets per reload. The rockets are notably less accurate than the Calliope, necessitating they be used from a closer range, but have the potential of dealing high amounts of damage to both vehicles and infantry in a short space of time, due to their greater blast damage and rapid rate of fire. The turret is also equipped with a 47mm Tank Gun and coaxial MG for threats at long range. The three other machine gunners operate weapons from the front left and right of the hull, and from atop the tank turret, respectively. Although an upgrade in terms of armament and general versatility, the HaChi retains much of its other statistics with the Type 97, including a lower profile versus Shermans. When matched against the Calliope, the HaChi warrants a more aggressive playstyle as it trades increased burst damage, mobility and p

Naeem was a Warlord who had left her bloodstained path in Old Russia to start anew. Discovering the location of the Ahamkara Hefnd's remains from Lord Shaxx, she befriends the Ahamkara and uses his power to grant wishes to villages in the European Dead Zone. However, she is killed by the House of Kings after they attack her fortress. In her final breath, she makes a wish that her vengeance follows them into the grave. This wish would be fulfilled decades later when Hefnd would raise the dead House of Kings members as Scorn.

Oryx, the Taken King, born Aurash and formerly known as Auryx (meaning "Long Thought"), was the sovereign of the Osmium Throne, the God-King of the Hive, and the master of the Taken. Reborn in the Darkness itself through a wicked pact with the Worm Gods, Oryx is the founder of the Hive race alongside his sisters and fellow deities, Savathûn, the Witch Queen and Xivu Arath, God of War. Of all the Hive gods, he alone held the power to bend other races to his will through the power to Take. Oryx is also the father of the dreaded Crota, a deadly Hive Prince who slew thousands of Guardians during the Great Disaster, Nokris, his estranged firstborn and herald of the Worm God Xol, as well as two Deathsingers and inventors of the Oversoul, twins Ir Anûk and Ir Halak. Enraged at the death of Crota, Oryx traveled to the Sol System aboard his Dreadnaught seeking revenge but was defeated by the Guardian and escaped to his throne world. His second match with the Guardians resulted in his permanent death and ended the threat he posed to the Sol System, leaving behind a vacancy on his Osmium throne that would remain empty for years to come.

Omnigul, Will of Crota was an Ascendant Hive Wizard and the consort of the Hive god Crota; she was also the matron of the Spawn of Crota and the leader of his armies. She acted as the secondary antagonist of The Dark Below campaign, where she led the Hive in resurrecting Crota back to the material realm and raising an army to invade the City; both efforts were thwarted as she finally met her end at the hands of a Fireteam of Guardians led by the Guardian.

The Iowa-class Battleship was a class of six fast battleships used by the United States Navy brought into service during World War II. Built to a 45,000-long-ton displacement limit, in the Pacific Theater they served primarily as fast escorts for Essex-class aircraft carriers of the Fast Carrier Task Force and also shelled Japanese positions. The four Iowa-class ships built were the last battleships commissioned in the US Navy, with all older US battleships being decommissioned by 1947. Missouri and Wisconsin last saw action in the Gulf War of 1991.

Optus Vocca is a Cabal Psion of the Imperial Cabal who serves as an Optus and is one of the Imperial Generals who volunteered to defend the champion of Cabal, Ignovun, Chosen of Caiatl. They are slain by a group of Guardians inside the Halphas Electus during the Proving Grounds Strike.

Oxiith, Abandoned Spawn is a Hive Wizard who serves as the boss of the lunar Haunted Sector of Year 4's Festival of the Lost. Oxiith is assumed responsible for the magic involving the summoning circles of Headless One's within the sector. Ikora Rey tasks Guardians with killing them.
Optus Haseth, Coalition Ally is a Psion Optus of the Imperial Cabal. They can be found in the Pleasure Gardens area aboard the Derelict Leviathan, being held prisoner by a Loyalist Shield Warden.

The Hummel (German; Bumblebee) was a self-propelled artillery vehicle used by the Wehrmacht during World War II. Based on the Panzer IV, the vehicle mounted a 15cm howitzer in an open-top superstructure. Entering service in 1943, around 700 were produced.

Nuajes, Hacking Psion is an Imperial Cabal Psion sent by Empress Caiatl alongside Decima, Shielding Psion and Thysaeuc, Quicksilver Psion to assist the Guardian in breaching Bunker WAR-6 to stop Maya Sundaresh from using a Warsat to expand the influence of her Echo of Command.
Pirrha, the Rifleman is a Baron of the Scorn who specialized in long-range combat.

Phylaks, the Warrior was a Fallen Baroness from the House of Salvation and one of the most trusted lieutenants for Eramis, Kell of Darkness. Born of the House of Devils, Phylaks would rally under the banner of House Salvation to aid in Eramis' campaign following her escape from the Prison of Elders. She was a skilled Stasis wielder and was as lethal as loyal; she stopped at nothing to advance Eramis's cause.
Having a Blast is a Player Card featured in Battlefield 2042. It is unlocked by inflicting 100 damage on vehicles with Anti-Tank Mines and 100 damage on vehicles with C5.

Praksis, the Technocrat is a Fallen Baron from the House of Salvation and one of the most trusted lieutenants for Eramis. Born into the House of Wolves, Praksis joined Eramis's quest to start a new world following their escape from the Prison of Elders. He is as lethal as loyal and will stop at nothing to advance Eramis's cause. As chief architect and scientist of the House, Praksis created the technology that helped the House of Salvation wield the power of Stasis. His research on Clovis Bray's Exo program laid the foundations for future Eliksni to harness that power. His fascination for machines developed into a deep admiration for the Vex and to the point that he conducted twisted experiments on them to improve Eliksni technology. Following his death and the events of The Witch Queen, Praksis would be resurrected as a Stasis-infused Scorn monstrosity by the Witness, serving as the final boss of Operation: Seraph's Shield Exotic Mission.

Pom is the Ghost of the Hunter Marin Mansanas. During her duel with Pirrha, the Rifleman to save the life of Errol Mayz, Marin would instruct Pom to not come out no matter what, knowing the Rifleman's love for collecting Ghosts as trophies. Pom would confirm with a pulse of warmth in Marin's left hand.

Quantum Harpies are a stronger Elite variant of the Harpy seen throughout Vex controlled space. They can be distinguished from their Minor counterparts by their more silvery appearance. In the Sol Divisive, they sport a healthier, greener foliage.

Rajesh was a member of the Future War Cult during the Golden Age who participated in experiments with a device based on Vex technology that allowed its user to send their mind across space and time.
Qalec was a Psion of the Imperial Cabal and a member of Yirix's conspiracy to assassinate Commander Zavala to complete Amtec's mission to avenge the deaths of Niruul, Ozletc, and Tazaroc.
Qinziq was a Psion officer who served Emperor Calus. She helped oversee a project that connected the minds of captured Scorn to the Crown of Sorrow in a bid to help Calus commune with the Darkness.

Prosperous Minotaurs are a variant of Major Vex Minotaurs that are encountered within Gambit, and formerly Gambit Prime, as High-Value Targets. They are surrounded by a distinct, white aura that sets them apart from the other Minotaurs.
The Ravenous Dire Minotaur is a more durable variant of the Dire Minotaur.
Rudoc, Imprisoned Flayer was a Psion Flayer seen with a pair of other Psion Flayers in the Fields of Glass on Mercury during the Flashpoint.

Rhungatt, Might of Xivu Arath was a Hive Ogre encountered in the story mission, Cocoon. It was called upon for reinforcements alongside several other Hive of Xivu Arath in an attempt to impede the player from progressing further through the Dreaming City in order to find Osiris.
The Resonant Shepherd is a giant Ultra variant of the Scorn Chieftain.

Savek, Betrayer for Xivu Arath was a Fallen and a former associate for the House of Spider syndicate. She was a part of the salvage crew tasked with scavenging the remains of a Ketch from the House of Kings. Alongside Kosis, she was among the first to discover the rise of Cryptoliths around the Tangled Shore. Later she was corrupted into a Wrathborn, and in the process was transformed from a Dreg into a four-armed monstrosity with the stature of an Archon.
A Heavy Barrel is a weapon attachment used to increase a weapon's accuracy by reducing barrel whip.

Shadow Guard Legionaries are powerful members of the Shadow Legion that fight as part of a special unit. They appear as both Elite and Majors, with the former sporting colors similar to the Legion's Elites and the latter donning the white of its Majors. They are highly aggressive and resilient, and are protected by Strand Absorption Shields.

Shadow Guard Incendiors are powerful members of the Shadow Legion that fight as part of a special unit. They appear as both Elite and Majors, with the former sporting colors similar to the Legion's Elites and the latter donning the white of its Majors. They are highly aggressive and resilient, and are protected by Strand Absorption Shields.

Skira, the Watcher was an ancient foe of the Eliksni who hunted them down before the arrival of the Great Machine on Riis. Skira was a shapeshifter and manipulator who preyed on the fear of the Eliksni which made it powerful. However, once the Eliksni ceased to be afraid of the shapeshifter, Skira ceased to exist.
Hovercraft may refer to: *LCAC - A vehicle featured in Battlefield 3 and Battlefield 4. *ACV - A vehicle featured in Battlefield 4. *LCAA Hovercraft - A vehicle featured in Battlefield 2042.

The Soulfire Hierarch is a powerful Hive Wizard who was sent to the Ruins of Wrath by Xivu Arath, God of War to conduct a ritual which involved using Soulfire in order to create a means of travelling directly between her master's throne world and the realm. However, she was killed by the Guardian and the ritual was disrupted.
Spectral Heralds are servants of Enkaar, the Anointed. They are encountered in The Conversation.

Soume, Deathsinger Trio is a Hive Wizard and Deathsinger of Xivu Arath's Horde striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They are accompanied by their fellow Deathsingers Tuis and Pritk. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.
"Holo" may refer to one of three weapon sights: *Holographic Sight, also known as Holo sight - An American sight. *PKA-S - A Russian sight. *HD-33 - A Chinese sight.

The Sinister Harpy is a Nessian Schism Harpy and one of Maya Sundaresh's Sol Sentinels tasked with overseeing the scavenging of the Plaguelands in search for Golden Age tech and Warsats to further her plans. It is encountered as one of the the potential final bosses of the Conductor's Keep version of Reclaim.

Syrok, Word of Oryx was an Ultra Taken Knight who took part in the assault of the Cabal Fleetbase Korus on Phobos, heralding the arrival of Oryx, the Taken King, in the Sol System. Syrok was among the first Taken to be encountered by the Guardian inside the Skyburners's base, who managed to survive the ambush and eliminate the Knight and its forces.

Ta'aun, Hand of Oryx, formerly known as Primus Ta'aun, was the commander of the Cabal Skyburners. He was bonded with the Shield Brothers Valus Tlu'urn and Valus Mau'ual and regarded as the mightiest cabal in the Solar System at the time. Nonetheless, he was Taken in action in front of the Guardian and reshaped into a servant of Oryx, the Taken King. He was slain, alongside Baxx, Hand of Oryx, while defending the path to the Taken King's chambers.

A hatchet is a small tool with a heavy chopping blade on one side and a hammer head on the back side. While it can be used for brute tasks such as splitting wood, its small size also makes it suitable for delicate tasks such as carving and shaving.

Sulmâkta, High Conductor is a Hive Wizard residing in The Scarlet Keep, who held power over the Deathsong. For this power, they were targeted by the Guardian as part of their Quest to weaponize the Deathsong. They confronted the Guardian in the Keep's elevator, but ended up slain.

Tagh'al, Blademaster was a powerful Gladiator who led a crew of Cabal and Fallen pirates, alongside his brother, Thagh'urn. He and his sibling served as the two final bosses of the Pirate Hideout: The Blademasters activity.

The Subversive Wizard is a powerful Hive Wizard in charge of creating a new nest for the Hive within K1 Logistics on the Moon. They are one of the final bosses of the Solo Ops activity Solo Ops: K1 Logistics.
The Kübelwagen, short for Kübelsitzwagen which in English literally means "bucket-seat car" was the primary German military car in the 1930s used by the German military. __TOC__

Tevis Larsen was a sly Hunter and a friend of Hunter Vanguard Cayde-6, who described him as a "lying cheat". Apart from owing Cayde a large amount of Glimmer, Tevis was a well-respected and revered member of the Nightstalkers, a Hunter subclass which uses the Void to dispatch enemy forces quickly. He is also mentioned to have been good friends with Andal Brask and Shiro-4, as well as Cayde-6.
Thaltos, the Deathless was a Hive Knight seen in the Warsat Down Heroic Public Event in the Glacial Drift during the Mars Flashpoint.
Termiiks, Invasive Warrant is a powerful and agile Scorn Raider, as well as the warden of the Temple of the Cunning in Savathûn's Throne World. They appear as a boss in The Cunning Mission.

A Knife, or known primarily as a Combat Knife or Fighting Knife is a cutting weapon designed for military use, specifically for close combat; however, since the end of trench warfare, most military knives have been primarily designed for utility/tool use (clearing foliage, chopping branches for cover, opening ammunition crates, etc.). Knives are featured as melee weapons in several installments of the Battlefield series.
